verses.zh: 第七年五月初十日，有以色列的几个长老来求问耶和华，坐在我面前。
verses.en: In the seventh year, in the fifth month, on the tenth of the month,[NOTE:1] some of the elders[NOTE:2] of Israel came to seek[NOTE:3] the Lord, and they sat down in front of me.
notes: The date would be August 14th, 591 b.c. The seventh year is the seventh year of Jehoiachin’s exile.
Heb “men from the elders.”
See the note at 14:3.
verses.commentary:
20:1 "in the seventh year, in the fifth month, on the tenth of the month" Ezekiel makes an
attempt to date his prophecies (i.e. 591 B.C., cf. 2 Kgs. 25:8; compare with
Jer. 52:12; also note the dates in Ezek. 1:1; 8:1; 20:1; 26:1; 29:1,17; 30:20; 31:1; 32:1,17; 33:21).
The purpose for this may be

- a literary way of asserting that YHWH spoke to him

- a way of showing he was a true prophet (i.e. YHWH spoke to him before the event)

- just his meticulous personality or possibly priestly training

The elder's question is not stated, but the date causes one to imagine it was related to Egypt's
power and Zedekiah's proposed alliance with Pharaoh Psammetik II (595-589 B.C.).

Special Topic: ANE Calendars

▣ "the elders of Israel came to inquire of the Lord" They had done
this before (cf. Ezek. 8:1,11,12; 14:1). We do not know what they came to ask because Ezekiel receives
another vision while they sat there. This revelation relates to their questions.

Special Topic: Elder

verses.zh: 耶和华的话临到我说：
verses.en: The Lord’s message came to me:

verses.zh: 「人子啊，你要告诉以色列的长老说，主耶和华如此说：你们来是求问我吗？主耶和华说：我指着我的永生起誓，我必不被你们求问。
verses.en: “Son of man, speak to the elders of Israel, and tell them: ‘This is what the Sovereign Lord says: Are you coming to seek me? As surely as I live, I will not allow you to seek me,[NOTE:1] declares the Sovereign Lord.’
notes: Or “I will not reveal myself to you.”
verses.commentary:
20:3 The motives and sins of this (these) group(s) of elders are consistently negative (cf. Ezek. 8:1;
14:1). They came as if they were seeking YHWH's advice and guidance (cf. Ezek. 14:3; 20:31), but in reality,
they were idolaters (cf. Ezek. 14:7). The wickedness of Jerusalem (chapters 8-10) has already affected the
exiles (leaders reflect the populace). This uniform evil demonstrates that YHWH's choosing the exiles to
reconstitute Israel, while judging and destroying those in Palestine, was an act of mercy, not merit
(cf. Ezek. 36:22-38). He chose them because of His eternal redemptive purposes for all mankind!

One day YHWH will listen again (cf. Ezek. 36:37-38)!

Special Topic: YHWH's Eternal Redemptive Plan

▣ "Son of Man" See note at Ezek. 2:1.

▣ "speak" This (BDB 180, KB 210) is a Piel IMPERATIVE
(cf. Ezek. 3:1; 12:23; 14:4; 20:27; 29:3; 33:2; 37:19,21). Ezekiel passes on YHW's message, not his own.

▣ "the Lord God" This is literally Adon YHWH. Notice the number
of titles used for Deity in this chapter. This is a chapter about God and His intentions
for Israel, but they would not!

- Lord (YHWH), Ezek. 20:2 (see Speial Topic: Names for Deity, D.)

- Adon YHWH, Ezek. 20:3(twice), 5,27,30,31,33,36,39,40,44,47,49 (see Special Topic: Lord (adon and kuiros)

- YHWH your Elohim, Ezek. 20:5,7,19,20 (see Special Topic: Names for Deity, C.)

- I am the Lord (YHWH), Ezek. 20:26,38,42,44

- I, the Lord (YHWH), Ezek. 20:48

Also notice the personal PRONOUNS and phrases.

- Myself, Ezek. 20:5,9

- against Me, Ezek. 20:8,13,21,27,38

- My wrath, Ezek. 20:8,13,21

- My anger, Ezek. 20:8,21

- My name, Ezek. 20:9,14

- My statutes, Ezek. 20:11,13,16,19,21,24

- My ordinances, Ezek. 20:11,13,16,19,21,24

- My sabbaths, Ezek. 20:11,13,16,20,21,24

- My eye, Ezek. 20:17

- My hand, Ezek. 20:22

- blasphemed Me, Ezek. 20:27

- listen to Me, Ezek. 20:39

- My holy name, Ezek. 20:39

- My holy mountain, Ezek. 20:40

- serve Me, Ezek. 20:40

- prove Myself holy, Ezek. 20:41

- My name's sake, Ezek. 20:44

verses.zh: 人子啊，你要审问审问他们吗？你当使他们知道他们列祖那些可憎的事，
verses.en: Are you willing to pronounce judgment on them?[NOTE:1] Are you willing to pronounce judgment, son of man? Then confront them with the abominable practices of their fathers,
notes: Heb “will you judge.” Here the imperfect form of the verb is probably used with a desiderative nuance. Addressed to the prophet, “judge” means to warn of or pronounce God’s impending judgment.
verses.commentary:
20:4 YHWH seems to be asking Ezekiel if he is ready to act as His mouthpiece in confronting (cf. Ezek. 16:2; 22:2)
these idolatrous elders. The repeated VERB "judge" (BDB 1047; KB 1622) could be Qal IMPERFECT
or Qal IMPERFECT used as a JUSSIVE (cf. Ezek. 20:7,18 [thrice]).

▣ "Make them know" This VERB (BDB 393, KB 390) is a Hiphil IMPERATIVE
(Hiphil PERFECT in Ezek. 22:2). It implies both

- truth

- a relationship with YHWH (e.g. Gen. 4:1; Jer. 1:5)

▣ "abomination" See Special Topic: Abomination (OT).

▣ "of their fathers" This is surprising in light of Ezekiel 18. Are these elders being confronted because of their parents'
or ancestors' sins? Our parents and society often instill destructive patterns or licenses which reap judgment (cf. Exod. 20:5; Deut. 5:9,10).
There is both an individual and corporate ethical, moral, religious responsibility. It is not an either/or situation. These elders are affected, but
also responsible, as were the Davidic kings of Ezekiel 19.

verses.zh: 对他们说，主耶和华如此说：当日我拣选以色列，向雅各家的后裔起誓，在埃及地将自己向他们显现，说：我是耶和华―你们的　神。
verses.en: and say to them: “‘This is what the Sovereign Lord says: On the day I chose Israel I swore[NOTE:1] to the descendants[NOTE:2] of the house of Jacob and made myself known to them in the land of Egypt. I swore[NOTE:3] to them, “I am the Lord your God.”
notes: Heb “I lifted up my hand.”
Heb “seed.”
Heb “I lifted up my hand.”
verses.commentary:
20:5-7 These verses describe YHWH's actions/admonitions towards the descendants of Abraham, Isaac, and
Jacob ("the seed of the house of Jacob," Ezek. 20:5).

- "I chose Israel," BDB 103, KB 119, Qal INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT,
this election terminology, so common in Deuteronomy and Isaiah, occurs only here in Ezekiel.

- "I swore" (lit. "lifted hand"), Ezek. 20:5(twice), BDB 669, KB 724,
Qal IMPERFECT with waw (i.e. that I would be their God)

- "I made Myself known to them," Ezek. 20:5, BDB 393, KB 390, Niphal
IMPERFECT with waw

- "I swore," Ezek. 20:6, BDB 669, KB 724, Qal PERFECT (that I
would bring them out of bondage, out of Egypt, cf. Gen. 15:12-21)

- "that I had selected for them," Ezek. 20:6, BDB 1064, KB 1707, Qal
PERFECT (I would give them the land of Canaan, cf. Gen. 15:12-21)

- "cast away. . .the detestable things," Ezek. 20:7, BDB 1020, KB 1527, Hiphil
IMPERATIVE

- "do not defile yourselves," Ezek. 20:7, BDB 379, KB 375, Hithpael
IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE sense,
cf. Ezek. 18:15; 20:7,18,31; 22:3-4; 23:7,30; 36:18,25; 37:23

20:5 "swore" This is literally "lift the hand" and is used twice in this verse. This forms the central
theme of this chapter (cf. Ezek. 20:6,15,23,28,42): YHWH's gracious provisions and covenant promises in contrast
to Israel's repeated covenant failures (cf. Psalm 106; Nehemiah 9).

The gesture of raising/lifting (BDB 669, KB 724) the hand can have several meanings.

- oath taking, Exod. 6:8; Num. 14:30; Ps. 106:26; Ezek. 20:5-6

- rebellion, 2 Sam. 20:21

- positive action, Ps. 10:12 (YHWH); 119:48 (human)

- blessing, Lev. 9:22; Ps. 28:2; 63:4; 134:2; 1 Tim. 2:8

- prayers, Lam. 2:19

Special Topic: Hand

verses.zh: 那日我向他们起誓，必领他们出埃及地，到我为他们察看的流奶与蜜之地；那地在万国中是有荣耀的。
verses.en: On that day I swore[NOTE:1] to bring them out of the land of Egypt to a land that I had picked out[NOTE:2] for them, a land flowing with milk and honey,[NOTE:3] the most beautiful of all lands.
notes: Heb “I lifted up my hand to them.”
Or “searched out.” The Hebrew word is used to describe the activity of the spies in “spying out” the land of Canaan (Num 13-14); cf. KJV “I had espied for them.”

The phrase “a land flowing with milk and honey,” a figure of speech describing the land’s abundant fertility, occurs in v. 15 as well as Exod 3:8, 17; 13:5; 33:3; Lev 20:24; Num 13:27; Deut 6:3; 11:9; 26:9; 27:3; Josh 5:6; Jer 11:5; 32:23 (see also Deut 1:25; 8:7-9).
verses.commentary:
20:6 "to bring them out" This VERB (BDB 422, KB 425, Hiphil
INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT, cf. Ezek. 20:6,9,10, 14,22,34,38,41) is often used
(in the Hiphil) of YHWH's act of

- prophetic fulfillment (cf. Gen. 15:12-21)

- mercy in delivering Israel from Egypt.

It is also used of YHWH delivering Israel from the Assyrian and Babylonian exiles (cf.
Ezek. 20:34,38,41; 34:13).

NASB
"that I had selected for them"

NKJV, NRSV
"that I had searched out for them"

TEV
"I had chosen for them"

NJB
"which I had reconnoitered for them"

LXX
"that I spied for them"

REV, JPSOA
"that I had sought out for them"

Peshitta
"that I given to them"

The VERB (BDB 1064, KB 1707, Qal PERFECT)
means "to seek out," "to spy out," or "to explore," in light of the fact that

- it is used so often for the twelve spies (cf. Num. 13:2,16,17,25,32; 14:6,7, 34,36,38)

- it is found only here in the Prophets.

The translation "spy out" seems best in light of Deut. 1:33. YHWH took special, personal care of young
Israel (cf. Ezekiel 16)!

▣ "flowing with milk and honey" This phrase is first used in Exod. 3:8,17; 13:5; 33:3; Lev. 20:24;
Num. 13:27; 14:8; 16:13-14. It became a technical name used in Aramaic sources (i.e. Persian) for the land of
Palestine/ Canaan (cf. Jer. 3:19). It was a very fertile place (cf. Ezek. 20:15).

NASB, NKJV, Peshitta
"the glory"

NRSV
"the most glorious"

TEV
"the finest"

NJB
"the loveliest"

JPSOA, REB
"the fairest"

LXX
"it is a honeycomb"

The MT has "the gazelle" (BDB 840 II, cf. v. 15), which was an idiom for beauty. The LXX seems to
relate the root to another root for "honey."

verses.zh: 我对他们说，你们各人要抛弃眼所喜爱那可憎之物，不可因埃及的偶像玷污自己。我是耶和华―你们的　神。
verses.en: I said to them, “Each of you must get rid of the detestable idols you keep before you,[NOTE:1] and do not defile yourselves with the idols of Egypt; I am the Lord your God.”
notes: Heb “each one, the detestable things of his eyes, throw away.” The Pentateuch does not refer to the Israelites worshiping idols in Egypt, but Josh 24:14 appears to suggest that they did so.
verses.commentary:
20:7,8 "cast away" This VERB (BDB 1020, KB 1527, Hiphil
IMPERATIVE) is often used of people rejecting God's revelation, word (cf. NIDOTTE,
vol. 4, p. 127).

- 1 Kgs. 14:9, Jeroboam I cast YHWH behind his back (i.e. out of sight, out of mind)

- Neh. 9:26, Israelites, during the period of the Judges, cast God's law behind their backs

- Ps. 2:3, the kings of the earth reject the Lord's anointed

- Ps. 50:17, the wicked reject YHWH's word

- Ezek. 23:35, Judah forgot YHWH and cast Him behind their backs

What these rebels should have cast away was their rebellion (cf. Ezek. 18:31; 20:7-8). One
day they will fling their idols out in the street (cf. Ezek. 7:19).

20:7 "defiled yourselves with the idols of Egypt" This could refer to the golden calf of Exodus 32 or the idols
mentioned in Josh. 24:14.

20:8a This describes Israel's rebellion against their covenant God (i.e. during and after the Exodus).

- they rebelled against Me, Ezek. 20:8 BDB 598, KB 632, Hiphil IMPERFECT
with waw

- they were not willing to listen to Me, Ezek. 20:8, "listen," BDB 1033, KB 1570, Qal
INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT, cf. Ezek. 3:7; 12:2

- they did not cast away the detestable things, Ezek. 20:8, BDB 1020, KB 1527, Hiphil
PERFECT, cf. Ezek. 5:11; 11:21

- they did not forsake the idols of Egypt, Ezek. 20:8, BDB 736, KB 806, Qal
PERFECT, cf. Exodus 32; Ps. 106:19-23

The foolishness of idol worship is highlighted in Ps. 115:4-8; 138:15-18; Isa. 44:9-17; Jer. 2:27-28; 10:3-5; Hab. 2:18-19!

Special Topic: Idolatry

verses.zh: 他们却悖逆我，不肯听从我，不抛弃他们眼所喜爱那可憎之物，不离弃埃及的偶像。「我就说，我要将我的忿怒倾在他们身上，在埃及地向他们成就我怒中所定的。
verses.en: But they rebelled against me and refused to listen to me; no one got rid of their detestable idols,[NOTE:1] nor did they abandon the idols of Egypt. Then I decided to pour out[NOTE:2] my rage on them and fully vent my anger against them in the midst of the land of Egypt.
notes: Heb “each one, the detestable things of their eyes did not throw away.”
Heb “and I said/thought to pour out.”

verses.zh: 我却为我名的缘故没有这样行，免得我名在他们所住的列国人眼前被亵渎；我领他们出埃及地，在这列国人的眼前将自己向他们显现。
verses.en: I acted for the sake of my reputation,[NOTE:1] so that I would not be profaned before the nations among whom they lived,[NOTE:2] before whom I revealed myself by bringing them out of the land of Egypt.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “for the sake of my name.”
Heb “before the eyes of the nations in whose midst they were.”

Heb “to whom I made myself known before their eyes to bring them out from the land of Egypt.” The translation understands the infinitive construct (“to bring them out”) as indicating manner. God’s deliverance of his people from Egypt was an act of self-revelation in that it displayed his power and his commitment to his promises.
verses.commentary:
20:9-12 God's actions towards Israel during the Exodus and beyond (Ezek. 20:9c).

- I took them out of Egypt.

- I brought them into the wilderness.

- I gave them My statutes, I informed them of My ordinances.

- I gave them My sabbaths to be a sign between Me and them (a regular worship time and place, Exod. 31:13).

- That they might know. This Hebrew word (BDB 393, KB 390, cf. Ezek. 20:20) implies both

- a personal relationship

- knowledge about something

Special Topic: Know

20:9 Notice that YHWH has a concern for "the nations." Israel was meant to reveal YHWH to the nations (cf.
Ezek. 20:14,39; 36:22-38; 39:7). I think there is a direct link to Gen. 3:15; 12:4; Acts 3:24-26; Gal. 3:8-9!

▣ "I acted for the sake of My name" This idea that historical actions related to Israel defined the character
of YHWH seems to have begun with Moses' intercessory prayer in Exod. 32:11-14. It becomes a recurrent theme (cf.
2 Kgs. 19:34; 20:6; Ps. 23:3; 25:11; 31:3; 79:9; 106:8; 119:21; 143:9; Isa. 37:35; 43:25; 48:9,11; Jer. 14:7,21;
Ezek. 20:9,14,22,44; 36:21,22-38).

YHWH's choice, love, and care for Israel was redemptively purposeful! There was/is
an eternal redemptive plan: YHWH created humanity in His image and likeness for fellowship (cf. Genesis 1-2). See
Millard Erickson, Christian Theology, 2nd ed., pp. 377-381.

Special Topic: YHWH's Eternal Redemptive Plan

verses.zh: 这样，我就使他们出埃及地，领他们到旷野，
verses.en: “‘So I brought them out of the land of Egypt and led them to the wilderness.

verses.zh: 将我的律例赐给他们，将我的典章指示他们；人若遵行就必因此活着。
verses.en: I gave them my statutes[NOTE:1] and revealed my regulations to them. The one[NOTE:2] who carries[NOTE:3] them out will live by them![NOTE:4]
notes: The laws were given at Mount Sinai.
Heb “the man.”
Heb “does.”
The wording and the concept are contained in Lev 18:5 and Deut 30:15-19.
verses.commentary:
20:11 "statutes. . .ordinances" See Special Topic: Terms for God's Revelation.

▣ "by which, if a man observe them, he will live" This alludes to the promises of Lev. 18:5; Deut. 30:15-20
and Ezekiel 18 (cf. Ezek. 20:13,21).

Life on earth is both physical and spiritual, similar to John 5:40; 10:10. Life is far more than mere
physical existence. There is a quality of life that only God can give, which involves more than things or time.
Augustine put it well when he said, "there is a God-shaped hole in every person." This is the image, likeness of the
Creator, which only He can fill!

Special Topic: Keep

verses.zh: 又将我的安息日赐给他们，好在我与他们中间为证据，使他们知道我―耶和华是叫他们成为圣的。
verses.en: I also gave them my Sabbaths[NOTE:1] as a reminder of our relationship,[NOTE:2] so that they would know that I, the Lord, sanctify them.[NOTE:3]
notes: Ezekiel’s contemporary, Jeremiah, also stressed the importance of obedience to the Sabbath law (Jer 17).
Heb “to become a sign between me and them.”
Or “set them apart.” The last phrase of verse 12 appears to be a citation of Exod 31:13.
verses.commentary:
20:12-13 A brief content outline (compare with Nehemiah 9 and Acts 7):

- Ezek. 20:7-8 shows the rebellion of the people of God during the Exodus

- Ezek. 20:12-13 shows the rebellion of the people of God during the wilderness wandering period

- Ezek. 20:20-21 shows the rebellion of the second generation during the wilderness period

- Ezek. 20:24-25 shows the continual rebellion of the people of God even in the Promised Land

- in the midst of all this rebellion, God's grace and provision remain steadfast

20:12 "sabbaths" This term (BDB 992) is surprisingly mentioned several times in this chapter in correlation with
words for YHWH's revelation (statutes, ordinances, cf. Ezek. 20:11-12, 13, 16, 19-20, 21, 24). The exact reason is uncertain.
For a good brief discussion on the origin of the Sabbath see Roland de Vaux, Ancient Israel, vol. 2,
pp. 475-483.

YHWH created this planet with cycles of nature (night, day) and worship times (feasts, sabbaths). They
were initially given to regulate times of work and rest, as well as regular worship times, events, and feasts.

For Israel four things were crucial for a faithful follower.

- circumcision

- keeping the sabbaths

- regular attendance at the central shrine three times a year

- covenant obedience to YHWH's laws

Special Topic: Sabbath (OT)

Special Topic: Feasts of Israel

Special Topic: Circumcision

Special Topic: Keep

▣ "who sanctifies them" This PARTICIPLE (BDB 872, KB 1073, Piel
PARTICIPLE) is from the root term "holy" (i.e. set apart for service to YHWH). Israel was
made holy by God (cf. Exod. 31:13) in order to reveal holiness to the nations. Their holiness would be YHWH's way to
manifest Himself to the nations (cf. Ezek. 20:9,14,22,39; 36:22-38).

Holiness is a covenant position (i.e. related to YHWH), but also a call to holy living!

Special Topic: Holy

Special Topic: Holiness/Sanctification

verses.zh: 以色列家却在旷野悖逆我，不顺从我的律例，厌弃我的典章（人若遵行就必因此活着），大大干犯我的安息日。「我就说，要在旷野将我的忿怒倾在他们身上，灭绝他们。
verses.en: But the house of Israel rebelled against me in the wilderness; they did not follow my statutes and they rejected my regulations (the one who obeys them will live by them), and they utterly desecrated my Sabbaths. So I decided to pour out[NOTE:1] my rage on them in the wilderness and destroy them.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “and I said/thought to pour out.”
Heb “to bring them to an end.”
verses.commentary:
20:13 Israel sins during the wilderness wandering period (i.e. from Egypt to Canaan).

- They did not walk in My statutes, BDB 229, KB 246, Qal PERFECT, cf. Ezek. 20:16 (twice), 18, 19, 21,39

- They rejected My ordinances, BDB 549, KB 540 Qal PERFECT, cf. Ezek. 20:16,24

- They profaned My sabbaths, BDB 320, KB 319, Piel PERFECT

Special Topic: Terms for God's Revelation

verses.zh: 我却为我名的缘故，没有这样行，免得我的名在我领他们出埃及的列国人眼前被亵渎。
verses.en: I acted for the sake of my reputation, so that I would not be profaned before the nations in whose sight I had brought them out.
verses.commentary:
20:14 Again YHWH's concern for His name before the nations is emphaasized (cf. Ezek. 20:9,22,39; Isa. 48:9).
YHWH has a personal interest in Israel (i.e. the coming Messiah).

Special Topic: Messiah

verses.zh: 并且我在旷野向他们起誓，必不领他们进入我所赐给他们流奶与蜜之地（那地在万国中是有荣耀的）；
verses.en: I also swore[NOTE:1] to them in the wilderness that I would not bring them to the land I had given them—a land flowing with milk and honey, the most beautiful of all lands.
notes: Heb “I lifted up my hand.”
verses.commentary:
20:15 Here the reason for the forty years in the wilderness is explained. It was Israel's continuing sin (i.e.
idolatry [cf. Ezek. 20:16b, Qal ACTIVE PARTICIPLE] and other covenant disobedience).

verses.zh: 因为他们厌弃我的典章，不顺从我的律例，干犯我的安息日，他们的心随从自己的偶像。
verses.en: I did this[NOTE:1] because they rejected my regulations, did not follow my statutes, and desecrated my Sabbaths; for their hearts followed their idols.[NOTE:2]
notes: The words “I did this” are not in the Hebrew text but are supplied for stylistic reasons. Verses 15-16 are one long sentence in the Hebrew text. The translation divides this sentence into two for stylistic reasons.
Heb “for after their idols their heart was going.” The use of the active participle (“was going”) in the Hebrew text draws attention to the ongoing nature of their idolatrous behavior.

verses.zh: 虽然如此，我眼仍顾惜他们，不毁灭他们，不在旷野将他们灭绝净尽。
verses.en: Yet I had pity on[NOTE:1] them and did not destroy them, so I did not make an end of them in the wilderness.
notes: Heb “my eye pitied.”
verses.commentary:
20:17 Even amidst their sin YHWH limited His wrath so as not to destroy Israel (cf. Isa. 48:9). In my opinion,
so that Messiah would/could come from Abraham's line and fulfill Gen. 3:15! There has always been an eternal redemptive
plan for all humanity (i.e. Isa. 66:23). Israel was a tool, a servant in that divine plan (cf. Acts 2:23; 3:18; 4:28;
13:29)!

Special Topic: YHWH's Eternal Redemptive Plan

verses.zh: 「我在旷野对他们的儿女说：不要遵行你们父亲的律例，不要谨守他们的恶规，也不要因他们的偶像玷污自己。
verses.en: “‘But I said to their children[NOTE:1] in the wilderness, “Do not follow the practices of your fathers; do not observe their regulations,[NOTE:2] nor defile yourselves with their idols.
notes: Heb “sons,” reflecting the patriarchal idiom of the culture.
Or “standard of justice.” See Ezek 7:27.
verses.commentary:
20:18-26 Again we return to the issue of multi-generational sin. Ezekiel, chapters 18-20, are related by this theme.
If one generation rebels, YHWH tries to encourage and inform the next one. Tragically Israel continued its rebellion
through time. It ultimately resulted in the Assyrian and Babylonian exiles (the bondage of Egypt in another land).
Moses predicted this (cf. Deut. 4:25-31; 28:64-68), as did Joshua (cf. Josh. 24:19-20).

20:18-20 A series of commands expresses YHWH's intent for the second generation of the Exodus.

- Negative (Israel's reality), Ezek. 20:18

- do not walk in the statutes of your fathers, Ezek. 20:18, BDB 229, KB 246, Qal IMPERFECT used in a
JUSSIVE sense (Special Topic: The Path, The Way)

- do not keep their ordinances, Ezek. 20:18, BDB 1036, KB 1581, Qal IMPERFECT
used in a JUSSIVE sense (Special Topic: Keep)

- do not defile yourselves with their idols, BDB 379, KB 375, Hithpael IMPERFECT
used in a JUSSIVE sense (Special Topic: Idolatry)

- Positive (YHWH's hope), Ezek. 20:19-20

- walk in My statutes, Ezek. 20:19, BDB 229, KB 246, Qal IMPERATIVE

- keep My ordinances, Ezek. 20:19, BDB 1036, KB 1581, Qal IMPERATIVE

- observe them (lit. "do"), Ezek. 20:19, BDB 793, KB 889, Qal IMPERATIVE

- sanctify My sabbath, Ezek. 20:20, BDB 872, KB 1073, Piel IMPERATIVE

verses.zh: 我是耶和华―你们的　神，你们要顺从我的律例，谨守遵行我的典章，
verses.en: I am the Lord your God; follow my statutes, observe my regulations, and carry them out.

verses.zh: 且以我的安息日为圣。这日在我与你们中间为证据，使你们知道我是耶和华―你们的　神。
verses.en: Treat my Sabbaths as holy[NOTE:1] and they will be a reminder of our relationship,[NOTE:2] and then you will know that I am the Lord your God.”
notes: Or “set apart my Sabbaths.”
Heb “and they will become a sign between me and you.”

verses.zh: 只是他们的儿女悖逆我，不顺从我的律例，也不谨守遵行我的典章（人若遵行就必因此活着），干犯我的安息日。「我就说，要将我的忿怒倾在他们身上，在旷野向他们成就我怒中所定的。
verses.en: But the children[NOTE:1] rebelled against me, did not follow my statutes, did not observe my regulations by carrying them out (the one who obeys[NOTE:2] them will live by them), and desecrated my Sabbaths. I decided to pour out[NOTE:3] my rage on them and fully vent my anger against them in the wilderness.
notes: Heb “sons.”
Or “carries them out.”
Heb “and I said/thought to pour out.”
verses.commentary:
20:21-26 Israel did not obey, but rebelled against YHWH).

- They did not walk in His statutes, Ezek. 20:21

- They were not careful to observe His ordinances, Ezek. 20:21

- They profaned His sabbaths (cf. Ezek. 20:20), Ezek. 20:21

So YHWH

- resolved to pour out His wrath, Ezek. 20:21

- accomplished His anger against them in the wilderness, Ezek. 20:21

- withdrew His hand, Ezek. 20:22, cf. Ps. 74:11; Lam. 2:3

- acted for the sake of His name, Ezek. 20:22 (cf. Ezek. 36:22-38)

- scattered them among the nations, Ezek. 20:23 (cf. Ps. 106:19-27 describes the wilderness period, Ezek. 20:26-27 make the threat)

- dispersed them among the lands, Ezek. 20:23 (parallel to #5)

- gave them statutes that were not good, Ezek. 20:25

- gave them ordinances by which they could not live, Ezek. 20:25 (apparently from false prophets or faithless leaders; see full note at v. 25)

- pronounced them unclean (i.e. worship of Molech, child sacrifice, see Special Topic: Molech), Ezek. 20:26

- made them desolate, Ezek. 20:26

verses.zh: 虽然如此，我却为我名的缘故缩手没有这样行，免得我的名在我领他们出埃及的列国人眼前被亵渎。
verses.en: But I refrained from doing so[NOTE:1] and acted instead for the sake of my reputation, so that I would not be profaned before the nations in whose sight I had brought them out.
notes: Heb “drew my hand back.” This idiom also occurs in Lam 2:8 and Ps 74:11.
verses.commentary:
20:22 "I withdrew My hand" This idiom can mean

- YHWH chose not to punish (cf. v. 17; Ps. 74:11)

- YHWH chose not to help Israel (cf. Lam. 2:3)

- a prayer of Job (cf. Job 13:21)

verses.zh: 并且我在旷野向他们起誓，必将他们分散在列国，四散在列邦；
verses.en: I also swore[NOTE:1] to them in the wilderness that I would scatter them among the nations and disperse them throughout the lands.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “I lifted up my hand.”
Though the Pentateuch does not seem to know of this episode, Ps 106:26-27 may speak of God’s oath to exile the people before they had entered Canaan.

verses.zh: 因为他们不遵行我的典章，竟厌弃我的律例，干犯我的安息日，眼目仰望他们父亲的偶像。
verses.en: I did this[NOTE:1] because they did not observe my regulations, they rejected my statutes, they desecrated my Sabbaths, and their eyes were fixed on[NOTE:2] their fathers’ idols.
notes: The words “I did this” are not in the Hebrew text but are supplied for stylistic reasons. Verses 23-24 are one long sentence in the Hebrew text. The translation divides this sentence into two for stylistic reasons.
Or “they worshiped” (NCV, TEV, CEV); Heb “their eyes were on” or “were after” (cf. v. 16).

verses.zh: 我也任他们遵行不美的律例，谨守不能使人活着的恶规。
verses.en: I also gave[NOTE:1] them decrees[NOTE:2] that were not good and regulations by which they could not live.
notes: Or “permitted.” sn The content of the verse is shocking: that God would “give” bad decrees. This probably does not refer to the Mosaic law but to the practices of the Canaanites who were left in the land in order to test Israel. See Judg 2:20-23, the note on “decrees” here in Ezek 20:25, and the note on “pass through the fire” in v. 26.

The Hebrew term חֻקּוֹת (khuqqot; translated “statutes” elsewhere in this chapter) is normally feminine. Here Ezekiel changes the form to masculine: חֻקִּים (khuqqim). Further, they are not called “my decrees” as vv. 11 and 13 refer to “my statutes.” The change is a signal that Ezekiel is not talking about the same statutes in vv. 11 and 13, which lead to life.
verses.commentary:
20:25 "I also gave them statutes that were not good and ordinances by which they could not live" This verse
has been a great concern to many commentators because it seems to impugn God's character.

- Rashi says that YHWH let their inner evil loose (cf. Ps. 81:12; Isa. 66:4; Rom. 1:24, 26, 28).

- Kimchi, another Jewish expositor, says that they were given over to the enemy (i.e. Canaanite tribes) and
they tried to live by their standards (i.e. worship of Molech, cf. Ezek. 20:26).

- This may be sarcasm, like Ezek. 20:29 and 39; they were using His guidelines (cf. Ezek. 20:11-13,16,19-21,24)
in Canaanite ways (one example, Genesis 22 became a model for child sacrifice, cf. Ezek. 20:26). These
people had the appearance of being faithful worshipers (like the elders of Ezek. 20:1-4), but in reality
were idolaters (cf. Isa. 29:13-14).

- The IVP Bible Background Commentary (OT), p. 706, mostly written by John H. Walton, gives several key grammatical
and lexical insights.

- he says this does not refer to the laws given at Mt. Sinai

- the word "torah" is not used

- the word "statutes" in v. 24 is FEMININE, which is normal, but in this verse it is MASCULINE

- it is possible it refers to YHWH's "decree" related to Judah's judgment for covenant infidelity

- This verse refers to the prophecies and regulations given by false prophets who YHWH used as the cause of His coming judgment (i.e. Ezek. 14:9).

verses.zh: 因他们将一切头生的经火，我就任凭他们在这供献的事上玷污自己，好叫他们凄凉，使他们知道我是耶和华。
verses.en: I declared them to be defiled because of their sacrifices[NOTE:1]—they caused all their firstborn to pass through the fire[NOTE:2]—so that I might devastate them, so that they would know that I am the Lord.’[NOTE:3]
notes: Or “gifts.”

This act is prohibited in Deut 12:29-31 and Jer 7:31; 19:5; 32:35. See also 2 Kgs 21:6; 23:10. This custom indicates that the laws the Israelites were following were the disastrous laws of pagan nations (see Ezek 16:20-21).

God sometimes punishes sin by inciting the sinner to sin even more, as the biblical examples of divine hardening and deceit make clear. See Robert B. Chisholm, Jr., “Divine Hardening in the Old Testament,” BSac 153 (1996): 410-34; idem, “Does God Deceive?” BSac 155 (1998): 11-28. For other instances where the Lord causes individuals to act unwisely or even sinfully as punishment for sin, see 1 Sam 2:25; 2 Sam 17:14; 1 Kgs 12:15; 2 Chr 25:20.
verses.commentary:
20:26 "they caused all their first-born to pass through the fire" This refers to the worship of the
Phoenician fire god, Molech (cf. Ezek. 16:20; Lev. 18:21; 20:2-5; 2 Kings 17:17; 21:6; 23:10; 11 Chr. 28:3;
Jer. 32:35). This may have been a misunderstanding about the death of the first-born recorded in Exodus 12, 13 or
even the offering of Isaac in Genesis 22.

Special Topic: Molech

verses.zh: 「人子啊，你要告诉以色列家说，主耶和华如此说：你们的列祖在得罪我的事上亵渎我；
verses.en: “Therefore, speak to the house of Israel, son of man, and tell them, ‘This is what the Sovereign Lord says: In this way too your fathers blasphemed me when they were unfaithful to me.
verses.commentary:
20:27 Israel was meant to be a light to the nations (cf. Ezek. 20:9, 14, 22, 41), but idolatry turned their witness
into confusion, darkness, and blasphemy (e.g. "to throw accusations," BDB 154, KB 180, Piel
PERFECT). Their covenant disobedience was seen as "unfaithfulness" or even "treachery"
(BDB 591, KB 612, Qal INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT, cf. Ezek. 14:13; 17:20; 18:24;
20:27; 39:26) against YHWH.

verses.zh: 因为我领他们到了我起誓应许赐给他们的地，他们看见各高山、各茂密树，就在那里献祭，奉上惹我发怒的供物，也在那里焚烧馨香的祭牲，并浇上奠祭。
verses.en: I brought them to the land that I swore[NOTE:1] to give them, but whenever they saw any high hill or leafy tree, they offered their sacrifices there and presented the offerings that provoked me to anger. They offered their soothing aroma there and poured out their drink offerings.
notes: Heb “that I lifted up my hand.”
verses.commentary:
20:28 "which I swore to give them" This refers to the repeated promise by YHWH to give Abraham and his seed the
Promised Land (i.e. Canaan).

- Abraham, Gen. 12:1,7; 13:15; 15:18

- Isaac, Gen. 50:24; Exod. 13:11; 33:1; Num. 11:12; 14:23; 32:11; Deut. 1:8; 9:5; 29:13

- Jacob, Gen. 26:3

- Israel, Num. 14:16; Deut. 4:21; 6:23; 8:1; 11:9; 19:8; 26:3,15; 28:11; 31:7,23; 34:4; Josh. 1:6; 21:43-44

Special Topic: Covenant Promises to the Patriarchs

▣ "then they saw every high hill and every leafy tree" This refers to the worship of the gods
of the Canaanite fertility cult of Ba'al and Asherah/Astarte. They turned every hill and valley into a place of sexual idolatry
(i.e. imitation magic, cf. Ezek. 6:13; 16:23-29; Isa. 57:5-8; Jer. 2:20; 3:6,13; 17:2; Hosea 4:13).

Special Topic: Fertility Worship of the Ancient Near East

Special Topic: Asherah

NASB, NRSV
"the provocation"

NKJV
"provoked Me"

TEV
"made Me angry"

NJB
"provoked My anger"

REB
"roused my anger"

The term (BDB 495) means "vexation" or "anger." It often refers to YHWH's anger at idolatry (cf. 1 Kgs. 15:30;
21:22; 2 Kgs. 23:26; see Special Topic: Idolatry).

The phrase "they poured out their libations" is mentioned as part of pagan rituals which provoked YHWH several times
in Jeremiah (cf. Jer. 7:18; 19:13; 32:29; 44:17-19). YHWH is a jealous God (cf. Lev. 26:30-31). He will not accept rivals!

Special Topic: Jealous/Zealous

▣ "soothing aroma" This (BDB 629) is imagery for an acceptable sacrifice (incense or meat, cf. Gen. 8:21; Exod. 29:18,25,41;
Lev. 1:9,13,17; Ezek. 6:13; 16:19; 20:28). It must be stated that this phrase does not imply that sacrifices were seen as a "feeding" of YHWH,
which is part of the Mesopotamian texts (i.e. Gilgamesh Epic). It is an idiom!

Special Topic: A Soothing Aroma

▣ "poured out their libations" This refers to liquid offerings (usually wine),
which often accompanied other sacrifices.

Special Topic: Alcohol (fermentation) and Alcoholism (addiction)

verses.zh: 我就对他们说：你们所上的那高处叫甚么呢？（那高处的名字叫巴麻直到今日。）
verses.en: So I said to them, “What is this high place you go to?”’ (So it is called “High Place”[NOTE:1] to this day.)
notes: The Hebrew word בָּמָה (bamah) means “high place.”
verses.commentary:
20:29 "Bamah" This is the Hebrew word for "high place" (BDB 119). Originally they were local shrines
(cf. 1 Sam. 7:17; 9:12-25; 10:5,13; 1 Kgs. 3:2-4) which were not condemned.

However, the same places became the sites of fertility worship (cf. Num. 22:41; 1 Kgs. 11:7;
12:31-32; 14:23; 15:14; 22:43; 2 Chr. 21:11; Jer. 7:31; 19:5; 32:35; Hosea 4:13; 10:8; Amos 7:9; Micah 1:5).
Josiah ordered them to be destroyed (cf. 1 Kgs. 13:2,32,33; 2 Kgs. 23:5-20; 2 Chr. 34:3-4). The centralization
of worship in Jerusalem (cf. Lev. 17:3-5; Deut. 12:13-14) was meant to control this potential abuse.

verses.zh: 所以你要对以色列家说，主耶和华如此说：你们仍照你们列祖所行的玷污自己吗？仍照他们可憎的事行邪淫吗？
verses.en: “Therefore say to the house of Israel, ‘This is what the Sovereign Lord says: Will you defile yourselves like your fathers[NOTE:1] and engage in prostitution with detestable idols?
notes: Heb “in the way of your fathers.”
verses.commentary:
20:30-32 The question is to whom does "your fathers" refer?

- immediate past generation

- wilderness wandering generation

- early settlers in the Promised Land

- or, collective of all past generations

The specific idols referred to are the fertility gods of Canaan (i.e. Ba'al, Asherah,
Molech). Verse 32 describes the enormity of the problem in the statement "we will be like the nations,
like the tribes of the land, serving wood and stone." Remember that the Israelites were given the land of
Canaan because of the continuing idolatry of the tribes of the land (cf. Gen. 15:12-21). If Israel repeats
their abominations, she will also be removed from the land (uniquely dedicated/owned by YHWH). Israel loses
that which makes her distinct! Israel cannot be a light to the nations because she has become one of the nations!
She was lost as a vehicle of revelation!

verses.zh: 你们奉上供物使你们儿子经火的时候，仍将一切偶像玷污自己，直到今日吗？以色列家啊，我岂被你们求问吗？主耶和华说：我指着我的永生起誓，我必不被你们求问。
verses.en: When you present your sacrifices[NOTE:1]—when you make your sons pass through the fire—you defile yourselves with all your idols to this very day. Will I allow you to seek me,[NOTE:2] O house of Israel? As surely as I live, declares the Sovereign Lord, I will not allow you to seek me![NOTE:3]
notes: Or “gifts.”
Or “Will I reveal myself to you?”
Or “I will not reveal myself to you.”

verses.zh: 「你们说：我们要像外邦人和列国的宗族一样，去事奉木头与石头。你们所起的这心意万不能成就。」
verses.en: “‘What you plan[NOTE:1] will never happen. You say, “We will be[NOTE:2] like the nations, like the clans of the lands, who serve gods of wood and stone.”[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “what comes upon your mind.”
The Hebrew could also read: “Let us be.”
Heb “serving wood and stone.” sn This verse echoes the content of 1 Sam 8:20.
verses.commentary:
20:32 This statement of desire by the idolatrous Judeans will never come to pass
(the Qal INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE and
the Qal IMPERFECT of the VERB "to be,"
BDB 224, KB 243). God's covenant people cannot be allowed to be like the other people. God desires that
He (the only true God) be revealed to the nations through His people! They are His people for this very
purpose.

Special Topic: YHWH's Eternal Redemptive Plan)

verses.zh: 主耶和华说：「我指着我的永生起誓，我总要作王，用大能的手和伸出来的膀臂，并倾出来的忿怒，治理你们。
verses.en: As surely as I live, declares the Sovereign Lord, with a powerful hand and an outstretched arm[NOTE:1] and with an outpouring of rage, I will be king over you.
notes: This phrase occurs frequently in Deuteronomy (Deut 4:34; 5:15; 7:19; 11:2; 26:8).
verses.commentary:
20:33 YHWH will not allow His covenant people to completely degenerate into idolatry.

- surely with a mighty hand

- with wrath poured out, cf. Lam. 4:11

These phrases (i.e. #1,#2) were originally used of YHWH's great and merciful acts of deliverance
(in the Exodus, cf. Deut. 3:24; 4:34; 5:15; 6:21; 7:8,19; 9:26,29; 11:2; 26:8; Josh. 4:24). But now they are
used to demonstrate that YHWH is fighting against rebellious Israel, not for her!

YHWH will be king (i.e. 1 Sam. 8:7)! He will accomplish His purposes through national Israel!
Even though He exiles them, He will bring them back into the land (cf. Ezek. 20:34,41; 11:17; 28:25; 29:13;
34:12-13; Deut. 30:3; Jer. 23:3).

verses.zh: 我必用大能的手和伸出来的膀臂，并倾出来的忿怒，将你们从万民中领出来，从分散的列国内聚集你们。
verses.en: I will bring you out from the nations and will gather you from the lands where you are scattered, with a powerful hand and an outstretched arm and with an outpouring of rage!

verses.zh: 我必带你们到外邦人的旷野，在那里当面刑罚你们。
verses.en: I will bring you into the wilderness of the nations, and there I will enter into judgment with you face-to-face.

verses.zh: 我怎样在埃及地的旷野刑罚你们的列祖，也必照样刑罚你们。这是主耶和华说的。
verses.en: Just as I entered into judgment with your fathers in the wilderness of the land of Egypt, so I will enter into judgment with you, declares the Sovereign Lord.

verses.zh: 我必使你们从杖下经过，使你们被约拘束。
verses.en: I will make you pass under[NOTE:1] the shepherd’s staff,[NOTE:2] and I will bring you into the bond of the covenant.
notes: This is the same Hebrew verb used to describe the passing of the children through the fire.
The metaphor may be based in Lev 27:32 (see also Jer 33:13 and Matt 25:32-33). A shepherd would count his sheep as they passed beneath his staff.
verses.commentary:
20:37 "pass under the rod" This refers to a shepherd's rod (BDB 986) used for counting sheep (i.e.
Lev. 27:32; Jer. 33:13).

NASB, NKJV, JPSOA
"into the bond of the covenant"

NRSV, NEB
"within the bond of the covenant"

TEV
"make you obey my covenant"

NJB
"bring you to respect the covenant"

REB
"counting you as you enter"

LXX, RSV
"bring you in by number"

Peshitta
"bring you into the discipline of the

covenant"

The MT is reflected in the NASB. The UBS Text Project, p. 60, gives it a "C" rating (considerable doubt).
The LXX, REB, RSV emend the word "bond" (מסרת; BDB 64, KB 608) to "by number"
(מספר; KB 607). Both make sense in this context.

verses.zh: 我必从你们中间除净叛逆和得罪我的人，将他们从所寄居的地方领出来，他们却不得入以色列地。你们就知道我是耶和华。
verses.en: I will eliminate from among you the rebels and those who revolt[NOTE:1] against me. I will bring them out from the land where they have been residing, but they will not come to the land of Israel. Then you will know that I am the Lord.
notes: See the note at 2:3.
verses.commentary:
20:38 The exile will "purge" (BDB 140, KB 162, Qal PERFECT)

- those who continue to rebel, BDB 597, KB 632, Qal PARTICIPLE

- those who continue to transgress, BDB 833, KB 981, Qal PARTICIPLE

▣ "they will not enter the land" See Ezek. 20:15, 16, and 13:9. Evil will be purged from the Promised
Land (and one day all the earth)!

verses.zh: 「以色列家啊，至于你们，主耶和华如此说：从此以后若不听从我，就任凭你们去事奉偶像，只是不可再因你们的供物和偶像亵渎我的圣名。
verses.en: “‘As for you, O house of Israel, this is what the Sovereign Lord says: Each of you go and serve your idols,[NOTE:1] if you will not listen to me.[NOTE:2] But my holy name will not be profaned[NOTE:3] again by your sacrifices[NOTE:4] and your idols.
notes: Compare the irony here to Amos 4:4 and Jer 44:25.

Heb “and after, if you will not listen to me.” The translation leaves out “and after” for smoothness. The text is difficult. M. Greenberg (Ezekiel [AB], 1:374) suggests that it may mean “but afterwards, if you will not listen to me…” with an unspoken threat.
A similar concept may be found in Lev 18:21 and 20:3.
Or “gifts.”
verses.commentary:
20:39-40 The verse begins with sarcasm (two Qal IMPERATIVES, "go" and "serve"), denoting Israel's
current idolatry. However, a new day is coming (i.e. "afterwards," BDB 29)! This is the great news of chapter 20. Judah has been so consistently
unfaithful, but YHWH is consistently faithful. He will restore a repentant and purged seed of Abraham!

Note how the text expresses this.

- You will surely listen to Me, Ezek. 20:39

- My holy name you will profane no longer, Ezek. 20:39, cf. Ezek. 36:21,22; Lev. 18:21; 19:12; 20:3; 21:6

- All Israel will serve Him, Ezek. 20:40

- I shall accept them, Ezek. 20:40

- I shall accept their sacrifices, Ezek. 20:40

- I shall accept them as an approved sacrifice, Ezek. 20:41

- I will gather them from the nations, Ezek. 20:41

- I shall prove Myself holy among you in the sight of the nations, Ezek. 20:41

verses.zh: 「主耶和华说：在我的圣山，就是以色列高处的山，所有以色列的全家都要事奉我。我要在那里悦纳你们，向你们要供物和初熟的土产，并一切的圣物。
verses.en: For there on my holy mountain, the high mountain of Israel, declares the Sovereign Lord, all the house of Israel will serve me, all of them[NOTE:1] in the land. I will accept them there, and there I will seek your contributions and your choice gifts, with all your holy things.
notes: Heb “all of it.”
verses.commentary:
20:40 "For on My holy mountain" In context this refers to Mount Moriah, on which Abraham offered Isaac (i.e. Genesis 22) and
on which the temple was later built (i.e. 1 Kings 7-8). This is a symbolic way of asserting the effective working of the Mosaic covenant.

The term "mountain(s)" (BDB 249) is used often in Ezekiel.

- It often is a way of referring to the whole land (as Mt. Seir stands for Edom, cf. Ezek. 35:2-3), i.e. Ezek. 6:3; 19:9; 33:28; 34:13,14; 37:22

- It often is a way of identifying the site of fertility worship, i.e. Ezek. 6:3-4,13; 18:6,11

- It refers to YHWH's special holy mountain (i.e. the temple), cf. Ezek. 17:22-23; 20:40; 28:14,16 (possibly a divine mountain in the north); Ezek. 43:12

The phrase "the mountains of Israel" is unique to Ezekiel (i.e. note repetition in Ezekiel 36).

Special Topic: Moriah, Salem, Jebus, Jerusalem, Zion

verses.zh: 我从万民中领你们出来，从分散的列国内聚集你们，那时我必悦纳你们好像馨香之祭，要在外邦人眼前在你们身上显为圣。
verses.en: When I bring you out from the nations and gather you from the lands where you are scattered, I will accept you along with your soothing aroma. I will display my holiness among you in the sight of the nations.
verses.commentary:
20:41 "As a soothing aroma I shall accept you" This CONSTRUCT (BDB 629 and 926) is imagery for a sacrifice
(see note at Ezek. 20:28). In Ezekiel it has been used consistently of pagan offerings (cf. Ezek. 6:13; 16:19; 20:28). But here it refers to the people
of Israel (cf. Ezek. 43:27). YHWH brought back the remnant from exile and denotes His acceptance of them by this priestly phrase (remember Ezekiel
was a trained priest of the line of Zadok)! A people in fellowship with their Creator has always been the goal of the tabernacle and Levitical sacrifices.

Special Topic: A Soothing Aroma

verses.zh: 我领你们进入以色列地，就是我起誓应许赐给你们列祖之地，那时你们就知道我是耶和华。
verses.en: Then you will know that I am the Lord when I bring you to the land of Israel, to the land I swore[NOTE:1] to give to your fathers.
notes: Heb “I lifted up my hand.”

verses.zh: 你们在那里要追念玷污自己的行动作为，又要因所做的一切恶事厌恶自己。
verses.en: And there you will remember your conduct[NOTE:1] and all your deeds by which you defiled yourselves. You will despise yourselves[NOTE:2] because of all the evil deeds you have done.
notes: Heb “ways.”
Heb “loathe yourselves in your faces.”
verses.commentary:
20:43 Israel's true repentance will cause them

- to remember (BDB 269, KB 269, Qal PERFECT) their sin (cf. Ezek. 16:61,63; 36:31, in Ezek. 6:9 they will remember how they hurt YHWH).

- to loathe (BDB 876, KB 1083, Niphal PERFECT) themselves for it (cf. Ezek. 6:9; 36:31).

verses.zh: 主耶和华说：以色列家啊，我为我名的缘故，不照着你们的恶行和你们的坏事待你们；你们就知道我是耶和华。」
verses.en: Then you will know that I am the Lord, when I deal with you for the sake of my reputation and not according to your wicked conduct and corrupt deeds, O house of Israel, declares the Sovereign Lord.’”
verses.commentary:
20:44 "not according to your evil ways or according to your corrupt ways" Grace, oh grace! What a marvelous message to share!
God will deal with us according to who He is and what He has done, not according to who we are or what we have done (i.e. Ps. 103:8-14)! Hallelujah.

The spiritual principle "we reap what we sow" is abrogated by the mercy and eternal redemptive
purposes of YHWH. Israel has a place in a larger scheme, as do the nations (cf. Romans 9-11).

verses.zh: 耶和华的话临到我说：
verses.en: (21:1)[NOTE:1] The Lord’s message came to me:
notes: Beginning with 20:45, the verse numbers through 21:32 in the English Bible differ by five from the verse numbers in the Hebrew text (BHS), with 20:45 ET = 21:1 HT, 20:46 ET = 21:2 HT, 21:1 ET = 21:6 HT etc., through 21:32 ET = 21:37 HT. Beginning with 22:1 the verse numbers in the English Bible and the Hebrew Bible are again the same.
verses.commentary:
20:45 A new revelation of a cleansing fire to sweep Canaan of idolatry. This parable introduces Ezekiel 21. This is where the MT starts a new chapter.

Special Topic: Fire

verses.zh: 「人子啊，你要面向南方，向南滴下预言攻击南方田野的树林。
verses.en: “Son of man, turn toward[NOTE:1] the south,[NOTE:2] and speak out against the south.[NOTE:3] Prophesy against the open scrub[NOTE:4] land of the Negev,
notes: Heb “set your face toward.” This expression occurs as well in Ezek 6:2 and 13:17.
Or “the way toward the south,” or “the way toward Teman.” Teman is in the south and may be a location or the direction.
Or “toward Darom.” Darom may mean the south or a region just north of the southern city of Beer Sheba. See M. Greenberg, Ezekiel (AB), 2:417-18.
The Hebrew term can also mean “forest,” but a meaning of uncultivated wasteland fits the Negev region far better. See M. Greenberg, Ezekiel (AB), 2:418.
verses.commentary:
20:46 "set your face toward" This is a literary marker for a judgment pronouncement (cf. Ezek. 6:2; 13:17; 20:46; 21:2; 25:2; 28:21; 29:2;
35:2; 38:2) which follows the same imagery used of YHWH (cf. Lev. 26:17; Jer. 21:10; Ezek. 14:8; 15:7).

▣ "Teman" This is one of three different words which denote the south.

- Temas (BDB 412, cf. Ezek. 40:24,27,28,44,45; 41:11,12,13,18)

- Darom (BDB 204, cf. Ezek. 21:2; 40:24,27,28,44; 41:11; 42:12,13)

- Negeb (BDB 616, cf. Ezek. 21:3; 40:2; 46:9; 47:19; 48:16,28,33)

All of these are allusions to the capital city of Jerusalem (cf. Ezek. 21:1).

verses.zh: 对南方的树林说，要听耶和华的话。主耶和华如此说：我必使火在你中间着起，烧灭你中间的一切青树和枯树，猛烈的火焰必不熄灭。从南到北，人的脸面都被烧焦。
verses.en: and say to the scrub land of the Negev, ‘Listen to the Lord’s message! This is what the Sovereign Lord has said: Look here,[NOTE:1] I am about to start a fire in you,[NOTE:2] and it will devour every green tree and every dry tree in you. The flaming fire will not be extinguished, and the whole surface of the ground from the Negev to the north will be scorched by it.
notes: The word הִנֵּה (hinneh, traditionally “behold”) indicates becoming aware of something and has been translated here as a verb.
Fire also appears as a form of judgment in Ezek 15:4-7 and 19:12, 14.
verses.commentary:
20:47 "it shall consume every green tree in you, as well as every dry tree" This parable describes a coming
judgment that will affect all Israelites. Here again, we are confronted with the two different ways of judgment.

- from father to children to the third and fourth generations, cf. Exod. 20:5; Deut. 5:9

- one individual's life does not affect the children, cf. Ezekiel 18

Somehow both are true! One deals with individuals and one with a national collective. The tension remains! For me personally, my
hope lies in Deut. 5:10 and 7:9! My nation may experience the judgment of God, which affects me, but My God knows me and will bring me (and my faithful descendants) to Himself!

verses.zh: 凡有血气的都必知道是我―耶和华使火着起，这火必不熄灭。」
verses.en: And everyone[NOTE:1] will see that I, the Lord, have burned it; it will not be extinguished.’”
notes: Heb “all flesh.”

verses.zh: 于是我说：「哎！主耶和华啊，人都指着我说：他岂不是说比喻的吗？」
verses.en: Then I said, “O Sovereign Lord! They are saying of me, ‘Does he not simply speak in eloquent figures of speech?’”
verses.commentary:
20:49 The idolatrous elders listening to Ezekiel (cf. Ezek. 20:1) heard these words and thought he was
speaking only figuratively. Chapter 21 is a reaction to this!
